category: flat-rate cloud storage with WebDAV, REST and MCP

free_tier.stated: 5 GB permanent on the free plan, plus 1 TB for 30 days once per account with no card. Paid storage is sold on a slider from 250 GB to 100 TB, priced per terabyte

per_object_cap.stated: 10 TB per file, with resumable transfers
per_object_cap.notes: the vendor writes 10 TB; the decimal figure is used as stated

retention.stated: Permanent on the free plan. The 1 TB trial is 30 days

egress.terms: No egress line item published; the page states '250 GB to 100 TB, priced by the terabyte and never by the head'

tooling: rclone webdav is named on the page, against https://drive.trekmail.net/dav/files/account/. A REST API and a 42-tool MCP server exist, and per-device WebDAV passwords are issued
chaining: A 10 TB per-file ceiling with resumable uploads, a REST API and MCP tooling is the only design in this survey aimed at programmatic bulk ingest by an agent rather than a human. The free plan is 5 GB, so the capability is priced and only the trial is free

limits.value: 10 TB per file, with resumable transfers

identity_cost.detail: an email address. The 1 TB trial is 'one-time offer per account' with no card

reliability_note: An email host that added a Drive product. drive.trekmail.net/status.php returns 404, so it is not a Nextcloud backend; /dav/files/ returns 401 on GET, so the endpoint exists and is auth-gated. The paid price is behind a slider and absent from the static page, which is why this is medium confidence

evidence.proved: '250 GB to 100 TB, priced by the terabyte and never by the head'; 'Biggest file 10 TB'; 'Up to 10 TB per file, resumable transfers'
'Server URL https://drive.trekmail.net/dav/files/account/'; 'rclone for scheduled backups, Cyberduck for parallel uploads'; 'One password per device'
FAQ: 'Yes: 1 TB free for 30 days, and no card. It is a one-time offer per account'; free plan 5 GB permanent
HTTP 401 on GET, so the DAV path exists and is auth-gated; status.php returns 404, so the backend is not Nextcloud

binding_note: The trial is 30 days and the free plan is 5 GB, so the clock is what ends it. The per-file ceiling is the number that would decide the plan if the price were known, and the price is behind a slider that the static page does not carry.
confidence_note: The paid price is not in the static HTML, so `price_per_tb_month` is absent rather than estimated.
notes: The design is right for a user and the free tier is wrong: 5 GB permanent and a 30-day terabyte. The paid ladder is unpublished in the static page, so no price is recorded rather than a guessed one. What would settle it is one order flow viewed end to end.
